## Why This Is Asked
Tests knowledge of VolumeSnapshot APIs, per-namespace scheduling, and how to surface status and logs from a snapshot operation while enforcing network boundaries.

## Key Concepts
- VolumeSnapshot and VolumeSnapshotClass
- Per-namespace CronJob scope
- ConfigMap as status store
- Logs via PVC mounted at /logs
- InitContainer for tooling installation
- Pod readiness/liveness probes
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
# CronJob skeleton
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: snapshot-app-data
  namespace: <ns>
spec:
  schedule: "0,30 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: init-tools
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl kubectl; sleep 0"]
          containers:
          - name: snapshotter
            image: my-snapshot-agent:latest
            volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-<ns>
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          nodeSelector:
            kubernetes.io/os: linux
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to orchestrate time-based batch workloads, integrate ConfigMaps and Secrets with PVs, and enforce idempotence and rollback for Kubernetes workload automation.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob with Job template and parallelism
- ConfigMap mounted as /etc/reconcile
- PVC mounted at /data/reconcile
- Secret-provided DB credentials via env vars
- Resource requests/limits and graceful termination
- checksum/config annotation to trigger updates
- RBAC: RoleBinding for service account

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: reconcile-cron
  namespace: data-warehouse
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            checksum/config: "abcdef1234" # placeholder hash
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: reconcile-sa
          containers:
          - name: reconciler
            image: my-registry/reconcile:latest
            envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: db-creds
            volumeMounts:
            - name: reconcile-rules
              mountPath: /etc/reconcile
            - name: reconcile-output
              mountPath: /data/reconcile
            resources:
              requests:
                cpu: "200m"
                memory: "256Mi"
              limits:
                cpu: "500m"
                memory: "512Mi"
          volumes:
          - name: reconcile-rules
            configMap:
              name: reconcile-rules
          - name: reconcile-output
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: reconcile-pvc
          terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

```yaml

apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  namespace: data-warehouse
  name: reconcile-cron-role
rules:
- apiGroups: ["batch"]
  resources: ["jobs"]
  verbs: ["create", "get", "list", "watch"]
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1

metadata:
  name: reconcile-cron-binding
  namespace: data-warehouse
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: reconcile-sa
  namespace: data-warehouse
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: reconcile-cron-role
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

kind: CronJob

kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: compliance-api-creds
  namespace: default

  token: <base64>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: secret-allowlist
  namespace: default
data:
  allowed_keys: |
    tls.key
    tls.crt
    creds
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secret-compliance-checker
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: secret-compliance-checker
    spec:

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical security hardening and disruption management capabilities for CKAD-level Kubernetes deployments.

## Key Concepts
- Container SecurityContext: runAsNonRoot, runAsUser, readOnlyRootFilesystem for container isolation
- PodSecurityContext: fsGroup for proper file permissions on PVC-mounted volumes
- Kernel capabilities: drop ALL to minimize attack surface
- PodDisruptionBudget: maintain minimum healthy pods during maintenance
- Rollout and rollback procedures for safe deployments

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-gateway
  labels:
    app: api-gateway
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: api-gateway
    spec:
      securityContext:
        fsGroup: 1001
      containers:
      - name: api-gateway
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10001
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop:
            - "ALL"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /srv
        - name: config
          mountPath: /etc/app
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: api-gateway-pvc
      - name: config
        configMap:
          name: api-gateway-config
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: api-gateway-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api-gateway
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills: multi-container pod design, InitContainers, PVCs, ConfigMaps, Secrets, TLS sidecars, probes, PDBs, and network policies, plus load validation and rollback strategies.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer for tooling setup
- PVC mounting and data direction between /data/events and /data/enriched
- ConfigMap/Secret for runtime config and credentials
- TLS sidecar for certificate rotation
- Readiness and Liveness probes
- PodDisruptionBudget
- NetworkPolicy for scoped egress
- Load testing and rollback workflow

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: config-aggregator-config
data:
  batchSize: "100"
  enrichmentEndpoint: "http://enrich-controller.analytics.svc.cluster.local:8080/enrich"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: config-aggregator-creds
type: Opaque
data:
  apiToken: <base64-encoded-token>
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: config-aggregator
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: config-aggregator
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: config-aggregator
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: init-tools
          image: alpine:3.17
          command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache curl jq; sleep 0"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /data
      containers:
        - name: worker
          image: myrepo/config-aggregator:latest
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: config-aggregator-config
            - secretRef:
                name: config-aggregator-creds
          volumeMounts:
            - name: events
              mountPath: /data/events
            - name: enriched
              mountPath: /data/enriched
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 9000
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 5
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /readyz
              port: 9000
            initialDelaySeconds: 20
            periodSeconds: 10
      volumes:
        - name: events
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: config-aggregator-events-pvc
        - name: enriched
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: config-aggregator-enriched-pvc
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt this for namespace isolation across multiple environments?
- What scaling considerations arise with batchSize tuning and backpressure?
- How would you observe and debug under intermittent enrichment endpoint failures?

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical CKAD skills: wiring ConfigMaps and Secrets, configuring InitContainers, implementing TLS sidecars, setting up readiness/liveness probes, and crafting a NetworkPolicy with conditional egress.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMap-driven feature flags
- Secrets for credential management
- InitContainers for tooling installation
- TLS sidecars for secure communication
- Readiness and liveness probe configuration
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: feature-config
data:
  ENABLE_API: "true"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: api-creds
type: Opaque
data:
  token: <base64-encoded-token>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: app-namespace
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: egress-policy
  namespace: app-namespace
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: internal-api
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 8080
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-app
  namespace: app-namespace
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: my-app
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: installer
          image: curlimages/curl:latest
          command: ['sh', '-c', 'echo Initialized']
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: my-app:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          env:
            - name: ENABLE_API
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: feature-config
                  key: ENABLE_API
            - name: API_TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: api-creds
                  key: token
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /status
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /status
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
        - name: tls-sidecar
          image: nginx:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 443
```

## Trade-offs
- **NetworkPolicy complexity**: The policy above allows egress only to the internal-api pod. A more permissive approach might allow DNS resolution but restrict target services.
- **InitContainer overhead**: Installing curl in every pod increases startup time and image size. Consider baking tools into the base image if startup latency is critical.
- **Sidecar maintenance**: A TLS sidecar adds complexity and resource overhead. For simple use cases, TLS could be handled within the application container directly.
- **Secret security**: Storing credentials in a Secret is fine for basic scenarios, but consider external secrets operators or vault integration for production environments requiring rotation.
- **Probe configuration**: Aggressive probe settings can cause unnecessary restarts; conservative settings may delay failure detection. Tune based on application startup time.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to coordinate init-time setup with a running app, ensuring idempotent migrations and safe rollbacks in a realistic CKAD scenario.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer orchestration and order
- PVC-mounted data initialization
- Probes for readiness/liveness under patch
- PodDisruptionBudget and graceful shutdown
- Rollback strategies in Kubernetes manifests

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal patch skeleton (illustrative)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: webapp
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: migrate
        image: migrate-image:latest
        command: ["/usr/local/bin/migrate"]
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /data
          name: data
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: webapp:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /data
          name: data
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "200m"
            memory: "256Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "512Mi"
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8080
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: data-pvc
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 10
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: webapp-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: webapp
```

- How would you ensure the InitContainer migration runs idempotently across restarts?
- What metrics or events would you monitor to validate rollout safety and rollback effectiveness?
